messages.author: 208520df5a1c57c2
messages.subject: Autocorrelated transects?
parts:
Imagine you are designing a survey with 2 strata using systematically placed
parallel lines. One stratum receives double the coverage of the other. All
transects will be oriented in the same direction. Would it be correct to
place a single transect grid over the entire survey area, but only fly every
second transect in the low coverage stratum? The advantage of doing this
would be less ferrying time, as the transects are contiguous across strata.
But this is what worries me. Is there an autocorrelation issue if a single
transect crosses 2 strata in a contiguous way, and is flown in one go but
divided into 2 transects for analysis?

Hoping this question is comprehensible,


Daniel Pike.

messages.author: 4cacbe3a86a908bf
messages.subject: Re: Autocorrelated transects?
parts:
Hi Daniel, List,

I believe that although strictly speaking the transects in the two
strata are not independent, the variance estimates within each strata
will be adequate, as within each strata you have a valid estimate for
the encounter rate (and its variance).

If you are worried about the global density variance, you could obtain
it using a bootstrap procedure in which, for each resample, if a line
was selected in stratum 1 and it continued into stratum 2 it would be
also selected in stratum 2. Care would be needed to ensure that you
obtained the same amount of effort in the two strata, but it should be
easy to do. This would have to be implemented in a bootstrap routine
outside Distance.

Cheers

Tiago
